subject: Burst slab reconciliation and procurement next steps
messages:
From: Chris Dobson <chris@optima-commerce.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@optima-commerce.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: burst week overrun — how will this be billed?

Sean,

We had a surprise spike during our campaign last week and exceeded our usual quota by ~3.2M tokens over a 48-hour window. Procurement asked me to get clarity on the overrun billing and whether Redwood has a short-window coverage option or emergency headroom to avoid a large one-off invoice.

Two quick questions:
- Will overrun be invoiced at pay-as-you-go rates for March, or can we apply the monthly committed rate as a one-time credit?
- Is there any short-window burst protection / temporary headroom you can enable retroactively while we formalize a PO?

I've attached the usage export from our side (Optima_Burst_Usage_Report_Q1.csv). If we need to escalate to procurement, please loop them in.

Thanks,
Chris
Chris Dobson
Head of Platform
Optima Commerce

Attachment: Optima_Burst_Usage_Report_Q1.csv (csv, 28KB)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Chris Dobson <chris@optima-commerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick: burst week overrun — how will this be billed?

Chris —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the usage file. Short answer: we can offer a retroactive short-window headroom and a blended true-up to avoid sticker PAYG for the entire overrun. I want to be clear about the trade-offs so procurement has what they need.

Proposal (high level):
- Enable a temporary burst slab covering the 48-hour window (retroactive entitlement) to absorb up to 3.5M tokens.
- True-up accounting: we will apply your committed monthly rate to 80% of the burst tokens and bill the remaining 20% at a reduced overrun rate (35% discount off PAYG).
- One-time administrative fee waived if you sign the short amendment/PO by end of next week.

I'll loop Ben for approval on the concession and Marissa for invoicing language. If that sounds reasonable we can push a 1-page amendment and I can start the DocuSign.

Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Sean / Chris —

Thanks for including me. I'm fine with the proposed blended true-up as long as we limit retroactive headroom to the specific incident window and record it formally (amendment + PO). A couple of guardrails I want noted:
1) Retroactive slab applies only to the 48-hour window in the CSV; future spikes must use the normal quota/overrun terms unless Optima signs a monthly headroom add-on.
2) The 80/20 split is acceptable, but we should tie the discount to a 6-month visibility commitment (e.g., 3-month rolling usage report + quarterly review) — just to make sure this was a one-off.
3) We'll offer a one-time 10% discount on the true-up amount if Optima commits to a 12-month smoothing addendum (optional).

Sean — please send the amendment PDF. Marissa, can finance generate a pro forma invoice showing both the full PAYG and the blended true-up line items so Optima can show it to procurement?

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Chris —

I've drafted a draft pro forma and attached it for review. The important bits for procurement:
- Line 1: Gross overrun at PAYG = 3,200,000 tokens x $0.0006/token = $1,920.00
- Line 2: Blended true-up adjustment = apply committed rate to 80% (2,560,000 tokens at committed rate $0.00035 = $896.00)
- Line 3: Discounted overrun for remaining 20% = 640,000 tokens @ 35% off PAYG = $249.60
- Net due (pro forma) = $1,273.60 (administrative fees waived per Sean's note)

If Optima can provide a PO by Fri 2027-03-05 and sign the 1-pager amendment, we'll apply the adjusted billing to the March invoice and reflect the entries on the same statement. Otherwise, default PAYG will apply and we'll invoice next billing cycle.

I've attached a PDF of the amendment and the pro forma (Optima_PO_31245.pdf). Let me know if procurement needs separate billing codes or an SOW line item.

Thanks,
